events.note:
Woldemar's death is most likely related to this: "On February 1, 1943, the 1st Battalion was disbanded and the 2nd/IR 458 was replacedallocated. The regiment was then transferred to the area south of Orel and used in defensive battles on both sides of the Orel - Kursk runway." (Grankino is south of Orel.)

About the 479th Grenadier Regiment:
"Created on October 15, 1942 by renaming the 479th Infantry Regiment and subordinated to the 258th Infantry Division . At the time of renaming, the regiment was in the Shanya position in the area south-east of Gshatsk. In January 1943 the regiment was in a defensive position between Yuchnov and Gshatsk and was deployed in the Rzhev area in the same month. On February 1, 1943, the 1st Battalion was disbanded and the 2nd/IR 458 was replacedallocated. The regiment was then transferred to the area south of Orel and used in defensive battles on both sides of the Orel - Kursk runway. In July 1943, the regiment took part in Operation "Zitadelle", the Battle of Kursk. After the German offensive was broken off, the regiment fought on the runway to Orel and withdrew from the Orel arc. In August 1944, the regiment was transferred to the southern section of the Eastern Front and used in defensive and retreat battles from the Mius via Stalino to the Dnieper. In February 1944 the regiment fought in the Nikopol bridgehead and withdrew from February to April 1944 via Nikolayev and Tiraspol to the Kishinev area. In March 1944 the 1st Battalion was disbanded. The III. Battalion was then renamed I. The regiment took up positions on the west bank of the Dniester. After fighting on the Prut, the regiment was crushed and destroyed in the Jassy pocket in August 1944."

- https://www.lexikon-der-wehrmacht.de/Gliederungen/Grenadieregimenter/GR479-R.htm

Note that the backsides of C1518 and C1519 state that Woldemar is buried in the Heldenfriedhof (German war cemetery) for the 258th Infantry Division in "Shernowez" (Chernivtsi, Ukraine, likely), grave number 59. This place may no longer exist in modern times, but more research is needed to determine this.
